races.name: Corinthian Amateur Jockeys' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Warning Sign
runners_data.note: Ran second over this exact 1m2f trip at Goodwood on good and won over 8f on soft last time out — the combo of trip, going and recent form points firmly to here; will take up a prominent berth and use race fitness to challenge late.|
runners_data.comment: Warning Sign arrives off a recent win and has experience of today's trip and conditions, making him a genuine threat at a fair weight of 157 lb from stall 2; the main risk is a 55-day absence since that victory.

runners_data.name: Epictetus
runners_data.note: Racing just five days after his last run, which is brisk for a hold-up performer — consistent place record on good ground but the short turnaround and natural rearward style leave him needing things to fall perfectly in a congested rear pack.|
runners_data.comment: Epictetus has been consistently competitive of late, finishing third last time out and second two starts back, and he has experience of today's distance and going. Carrying 155 lb from stall six, he's winless in recent starts but his profile makes him our pick here.

runners_data.name: Arcadian Nights
runners_data.note: Returns after 152 days off and has been exclusively running at 10f on standstill or soft, so the step up to 1m2f on good-to-firm is a double query; if fit enough, he travels up with pace and the 7lb claimer is a positive offset.|
runners_data.comment: Arcadian Nights has run over today's trip and going, and our rating puts him marginally top of these, making him a leading threat despite being winless in his last five starts — the main concern is the 152-day absence.

runners_data.name: Impierious
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner whose style-fit tag (0.92) reflects that this is his expected role, not an anomaly — three consecutive thirds at 8f on good suggest he stays up to standard but lacks a decisive finish; the test is whether he can control tempo and hold on.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent without a win in recent starts, Impierious has filled third in each of his last three outings; he has experience of today's going and steps up from stall three carrying 150 lb, though a rating of 80 leaves him with ground to make up on the principals.

runners_data.name: Beach Point
runners_data.note: Sharp winning form at 10f on good and a consistent placer, but this horse's true instinct is to hunt from the rear — mapped to midfield here because the hold-up berths are full, meaning it will likely race in a position that does not fully suit its natural rhythm.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with a string of fourths and an eighth offering little encouragement, Beach Point ranks sixth of seven on our figures — yet he has run over today's trip and going before and returns after 27 days off a manageable 148 lb.

runners_data.name: Drumstick
runners_data.note: Most recent winner in the field (1m2f, good, 94 days ago) and carries that form into this; genuinely held up in his races, and with the back of the field crowded his challenge depends entirely on getting an unobstructed passage — the 94-day absence is worth monitoring.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked last on our figures and returning after 94 days off, Drumstick is hard to fancy despite that winning effort last time out; he has distance and going experience in his favour, but the overall recent profile is patchy.

runners_data.name: What's The Plan
runners_data.note: Lightly weighted at 143lbs, consistent profile of placed efforts at 10f on good, and at three years old has time to improve; a natural hold-up operator racing into a bunched rear group, so needs a clear opening rather than a wall of horses to peel around.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent performer who has finished second and third in his last five starts, What's The Plan has run over today's trip and going and arrives fit on a 15-day turnaround; the main risk is that he remains winless in recent starts.

races.paceDynamic: Impierious is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger for the lead in a seven-runner amateur handicap, should be allowed to dictate a controlled, honest gallop over this 1m2f trip on good-to-firm ground. Warning Sign and Arcadian Nights will press forward to prominent positions behind him, creating a settled single-file shape rather than an aggressive early burn-up. The redistribution flag matters: Beach Point and Drumstick are true hold-up types who will find themselves competing for rear positions with What's The Plan and Epictetus, meaning the entire back half of the field is bunched with closers who cannot all get a clean run. This race shape — a lone front-runner setting a sustainable pace with a congested hold-up group in behind — strongly favours horses racing prominently just off the leader, as they avoid traffic, travel in the best ground, and can control their effort through the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Front Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Impierious dictates a fair but uncontested pace and the hold-up group fails to generate a late challenge.
scenarios.body: Impierious settles into an untroubled rhythm with Warning Sign and Arcadian Nights close behind, and the race is effectively run to suit those racing in the first three; the closers, trapped in a bottleneck, leave their challenge too late on the run-in.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Warning Sign or Arcadian Nights track Impierious closely and pick him off in the final furlong as the pace catches the front-runner.
scenarios.body: Impierious's inexperience (three consecutive third-place finishes) leaves him vulnerable to being run out of it close home by more experienced campaigners; Warning Sign, a winner over course-relevant trips, is best placed to exploit any fade.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Weaves Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to string the field out and create a gap for a late finisher to thread through.
scenarios.body: Drumstick, the most recent winner in the field, or What's The Plan would be the logical beneficiaries if traffic clears, but both are genuine hold-up types who must find a path; the congested rear makes this scenario structurally difficult to execute.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Swamp
scenarios.trigger: If Impierious goes too hard early under an inexperienced amateur and ties up inside the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A messy scramble develops through the final quarter-mile; Epictetus, consistent on good ground in this form cycle, and Beach Point have the staying profile to benefit, but both face the same traffic problems inherent in this field shape.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Impierious's amateur jockey Mr Henry Callan can regulate the tempo — if the pace is too slow it risks turning the race into a sprint finish that exposes Impierious, too fast and he ties up early.

Beach Point and Drumstick are both genuine hold-up horses forced to race closer than ideal; monitor how they settle in the early stages as any restlessness will cost them energy they need for a late finish.

Warning Sign has not run in 55 days and Gary & Moore yard is 1/19 in the past 14 days — if there is any fitness question from the layoff, his prominent position could turn into a liability rather than an asset.

Arcadian Nights returns from 152 days absent with no recent racecourse evidence; if Mark Loughnane has him ready the prominent berth suits, but the long absence combined with the softest recent going form makes him the biggest unknown in the field.

What's The Plan's 3-year-old claim over older horses at this trip is interesting given consistent 10f form on good, but the amateur jockey Mr Eireann Cagney will need to find clear daylight from the congested rear group early in the straight.

races.name: British Stallion Studs EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Beach Noir
runners_data.note: Posted a modest 8th and 14th in two Good-ground starts over 6-7f; holds-up by nature but the glut of hold-up types here means Rawlinson is likely to find it racing closer than preferred, reducing its already slim chance of landing a blow.|

runners_data.name: Catching Dreams
runners_data.note: Charlie Appleby's filly showed promise finishing second on Good ground over this exact 5f trip; Connor Planas has limited experience but the trainer's yard is firing at 7/18 in 14 days and a prominent position could unlock more.|

runners_data.name: Champagne Charlee
runners_data.note: Two unplaced runs at Haydock and Goodwood suggest she is still developing; a genuine hold-up type by inclination but with so many closers in this field she may end up forced forward, and Stuart Williams's 4/37 strike rate in the last fortnight offers little support.|

runners_data.name: Crazee In Havana
runners_data.note: Ran sixth over 6f on Good ground on debut; Oisin Murphy's presence is a huge positive on a track where his positioning out of the stands-side gate can make a material difference, and dropping to 5f may sharpen her up.|

runners_data.name: Kigali
runners_data.note: Three starts, best effort a sixth, never threatened on Good or Standard ground; likely to settle at the rear and face the same traffic issues as the other hold-up types, with Sean Bowen needing a perfect run through to get involved.|

runners_data.name: Menhaal
runners_data.note: Finished fifth and seventh in two Good-ground 6f races for Owen Burrows; has had 64 days off which could mean either freshening or rustiness, and Probert will be looking to slot in behind Elevating before making his move.|

runners_data.name: Pulse Of Fire
runners_data.note: Unraced to date for Ed Walker, who is in excellent form at 10/38 over 14 days; Kieran Shoemark is a significant booking and the complete unknown factor here — style, ability and temperament are all undeclared.|

runners_data.name: Elevating
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner; Richard Hannon's yard is striking at 10/59 and Sean Levey knows this Sandown 5f well — a second from six furlongs on Good ground shows Elevating can travel, and an uncontested lead makes this horse the race-shape fulcrum.|

runners_data.name: Vesper Honey
runners_data.note: Two-time tail-ender at Haydock and Goodwood with a tendency to fade in the finish; Jason Watson's booking is modest support and 38 days off adds another question mark — likely to be outpaced early and among the last to reach the rising finish.|

races.paceDynamic: Elevating is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner 5f maiden and, with no genuine rival likely to contest the lead, Sean Levey can dictate from the front at a pace entirely of his own choosing on Good to Firm ground at Sandown. The hold-up contingent — Kigali, Menhaal, Vesper Honey, Beach Noir and Champagne Charlee — will all be scrapping for the same rear positions, while Catching Dreams, Crazee In Havana and Pulse Of Fire are unknown quantities that could settle anywhere. The field holds more hold-up types than the race shape can naturally accommodate at the rear; Beach Noir and Champagne Charlee are the two most likely to be squeezed out of their preferred position and forced to race closer to the pace than ideal. A controlled, uncontested lead at 5f on fast ground strongly favours horses racing prominently or with a willingness to be close enough to track a single pacesetter — closers face an uphill task against a front-runner who is never pressured into going too fast.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Elevating Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Elevating is allowed to stride clear from the gates and sets an honest but unglamorous pace with no horse threatening to go past.
scenarios.body: Levey dictates every yard, keeps the fractions honest for a 2-year-old, and the race becomes a test of who can sustain their run into the rising Sandown finish; horses close enough to track gain maximum benefit from the slipstream.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Closers Capitalise
scenarios.trigger: If Elevating's early pace is fractionally faster than ideal and a prominent horse travelling sweetly delivers a smooth challenge in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A horse like Catching Dreams or Crazee In Havana, racing in second or third and conserving energy, swoops past a tiring Elevating close home; the Sandown uphill finish amplifies the effort of any horse with a clean line.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Swoop Through
scenarios.trigger: If Elevating goes faster than intended early and the field bunches, leaving a gap on the inside or rail for a hold-up type to thread through late.
scenarios.body: One of the overcrowded hold-up quartet — most likely Kigali or Menhaal — finds clear running at the two-pole and picks up the pieces as the front group ties up; this depends on pace being genuinely strong, which the current shape does not clearly support.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Exploits Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the redistribution of Beach Noir and Champagne Charlee causes early crowding and an uneven early gallop that scrambles the expected race order.
scenarios.body: A lightly-raced debutant or unknown quantity like Pulse Of Fire benefits from an unstructured race that levels the form lines; raw ability rather than tactical position decides the outcome and the favourite underperforms.

watchPoints.text: Elevating breaks cleanly — if Levey gets a smooth exit from the gates this race is effectively his to lose, and any rival that drifts wide or is slow away gifts him an unassailable lead on a track that rewards front-runners over 5f.

The redistribution of Beach Noir and Champagne Charlee into a crowded midfield is a live traffic risk — watch for bumping or interference in the first furlong as multiple hold-up types jockey for the same ground behind the sole pace-setter.

Pulse Of Fire's unknown profile is the principal wildcard; if Ed Walker's debutant shows natural speed out of the gates it could change the entire race shape by pressing Elevating and converting this into a true pace test.

Catching Dreams drops from 6f back to 5f — the same trip on which she finished second on debut — and if she travels close enough to Elevating early, the Sandown uphill finish could play squarely to her strengths.

Oisin Murphy on Crazee In Havana merits monitoring from a positional standpoint; Murphy is adept at finding ground on this track and if the prominent horses crowd each other out he is capable of threading through for a better-than-expected finish.

races.name: Chasemore Farm EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)
Hwfa Williams - Founder Of Sandown Park Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Elan d'Or
runners_data.note: Consistent front-running profile suits this lone-leader scenario perfectly; Stuart Williams has a 4/37 T14 but the horse's recent form includes wins over similar ground and this uncontested lead over 1m2f on Good to Firm is tailor-made, though stepping up from 8f trips is worth monitoring|
runners_data.comment: Elan d'Or showed his quality with back-to-back wins three and four starts back, and returns in good order just 19 days later with going experience in his favour; a placed effort last time out keeps him in the picture, and on a rating of 91 he heads this three-runner field.

runners_data.name: Interstate
runners_data.note: John & Thady Gosden's runner arrives on a solid 2/10f Good form line and the step to 1m2f looks a natural progression; the headgear (p) and modest T14 rate are neutral, and as the only runner with class to match the pace it sits as the key danger from prominent ground|
runners_data.comment: Twice runner-up in his last two starts, Interstate arrives here on a sharp 14-day turnaround with distance and going experience in his favour — a consistent threat. The main risk is that our rating of 73 suggests he may be flattered by his official mark.

runners_data.name: Edwin Hubble
runners_data.note: Brian Meehan's hold-up specialist has run well at 12f on Good ground twice (2nd and 5th) but the problem here is structural: in a three-runner race with a controlled gallop, there is simply no race to come from behind into, and Oisin Murphy's skill can only partially offset that tactical disadvantage|
runners_data.comment: Three times placed in his last five starts, Edwin Hubble returns on a sharp 12-day turnaround having run over today's trip and going, and a rating of 85 makes him a leading threat at 127 lb — though he remains winless in recent starts, which is the concern.

races.paceDynamic: Elan d'Or is the sole confirmed front-runner in this three-horse field and will control proceedings from the outset, setting whatever tempo suits connections over this 1m2f trip on Good to Firm ground at Sandown. With Interstate also mapped as prominent, both horses are likely to race in close proximity early, but the small field and lack of genuine pace pressure means this will be a tactical, controlled affair rather than a gruelling test of stamina. Edwin Hubble is the lone hold-up horse and will be forced to make ground from the rear in a slowly-run race with very few runners to weave through. This shape — a single unchallenged pace-setter dictating a moderate gallop — strongly favours prominent racers who can track and accelerate, putting Elan d'Or and Interstate ahead of Edwin Hubble, who will struggle to generate the finishing surge a hold-up horse needs when the pace is sedate and the field tiny.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Front, Clean Cruise
scenarios.trigger: If Elan d'Or leads comfortably and dictates a sustainable gallop that keeps the race tactical throughout
scenarios.body: Elan d'Or leads uncontested, conserving energy across Sandown's unique run-in, with Interstate unable to find an acceleration advantage from close range

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Interstate Tracks And Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Elan d'Or sets an honest enough gallop that the Gosden-trained Interstate can overtake in the straight with superior class
scenarios.body: Interstate sits a length or two off the leader and produces a clean turn of foot in the final two furlongs; the Gosden T14 strike-rate and OR advantage over Elan d'Or is the key factor here

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to string out the field and drain the two prominent horses before the final furlong
scenarios.body: Edwin Hubble, ridden by Oisin Murphy, finds room to close late if the front two have burned each other off; this scenario requires a pace dynamic this small field is unlikely to generate

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Rough Tactical Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the three-runner field produces unexpected early shuffling or Elan d'Or is checked, creating a scrambled and uneven gallop
scenarios.body: Any disruption to Elan d'Or's rhythm scrambles the predicted order but still leaves the race open to the two prominent types; Edwin Hubble's hold-up style remains the least suited regardless of the chaos

watchPoints.text: Elan d'Or's ability to dictate tempo unchallenged is the single biggest race-shaping factor — if it misses the break or is pushed wider early, the entire pace scenario collapses|
Interstate's trainer T14 rate (6/32) and its three-run form string (02-2) suggest it's competitive but not dominant — watch for whether Luke Catton tries to pressure the leader or sits patient|

Edwin Hubble's hold-up style is structurally disadvantaged in a three-horse tactical race; watch whether Oisin Murphy attempts to override the horse's natural style and race more prominently, which would change the shape entirely|

The going report confirms Good to Firm for this 1m2f race — faster than standard Good, which may suit the more prominent front-running types who can take advantage of the quicker surface rather than grinding closers who need give in the ground|

races.name: BetMGM 80s Day Saturday 29 August Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Desert Shadow
runners_data.note: Saeed bin Suroor's 4-year-old carries top weight on 142lbs but has an excellent record on good ground including a recent win over 8f, and hold-up tactics over this 7f trip on a flat, galloping track suit his profile ideally; visor headgear noted, 22 days since last run is fine.
runners_data.comment: Desert Shadow arrives in fine nick, winning last time out and second two starts back, with experience of today's distance and going working in his favour; the main risk is whether 142 lb proves too much of a burden.

runners_data.name: Tavana
runners_data.note: Sean Levey partners this lightly-raced 3-year-old whose most recent run was a solid 2nd over 7f on good ground, with the trip and conditions presenting no concern; trainer T14 strike rate of 1/5 is modest, but the horse's own form on similar going reads well enough to remain firmly in the picture.
runners_data.comment: Tavana shaped with promise when second last time out and has experience of today's trip and going, making her the one to beat off 135 lb from stall 2; winless in her last five starts, but that runner-up effort suggests a big run is imminent.

runners_data.name: Sunny Smile
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's filly has shown consistent placed form at 7f with two recent runner-up finishes, and her hold-up style suits a strong pace, though she will be held up less deeply than ideal given the congestion of hold-up types in this field — the slight compromise in position is a meaningful tactical caveat. Tongue-tie headgear noted; 33 days off carries no major concern.
runners_data.comment: Sunny Smile has been placed three times in his last five starts, finishing second on three occasions, and has run over today's trip and going — the profile of a consistent threat who keeps finding the line fast; yet to score in recent starts, and that elusive breakthrough remains the one question mark.

runners_data.name: Ascending Star
runners_data.note: Owen Burrows's 3-year-old is a confirmed front-runner whose last win came over 8f on good ground, but sharing the lead with Thursday Girl makes her task harder; trainer's T14 record of 0/11 is a notable negative flag. The energy cost of a contested pace duel is the central risk to her winning chance.
runners_data.comment: Ascending Star arrives here on the back of a win two starts back and shaped with promise when third last time out, and his experience over today's trip and a 34-day freshener make him a clear danger — the concern is whether 131 lb stretches his limits.

runners_data.name: Lunario
runners_data.note: Luke Dace's 6-year-old won over 7f on good ground recently and is in fair form, but his natural style is to be covered up at the rear — placed in midfield on this map because the hold-up berths are oversubscribed, meaning he is likely to race in a position that doesn't maximise his late finish. TV headgear; 26 days since last run is untroubling.
runners_data.comment: Lunario won last time out but that victory is bracketed by unplaced efforts, and he ranks fifth of six on our figures. He has run over today's trip and going, and 26 days between runs suggests reasonable freshness, but the weight of 130 lb makes him hard to fancy at this level.

runners_data.name: Thursday Girl
runners_data.note: Ed Walker is in sharp 14-day form (10/38) and Thursday Girl arrives here in excellent nick having won over 8f on good ground last time, with consistent placed efforts at 7f; she will fight Ascending Star for the lead and the outcome of that duel largely determines the race shape, making her a pivotal horse in any scenario.
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Thursday Girl faces a stiff ask, though she arrives in good heart — second in three of her last five starts, and a winner last time out — with experience of today's trip and going at least counting in her favour.

races.paceDynamic: Ascending Star and Thursday Girl are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the outset over Sandown's 7f, with neither likely to concede willingly — this creates a genuinely contested early gallop on good-to-firm ground that should produce an honest, end-to-end tempo. The pace battle between those two sets up a race that will stretch the field early and begin to sap stamina reserves from the front approaching the home straight. Desert Shadow and Tavana are genuine hold-up operators who will be best placed to exploit any pace collapse, while Sunny Smile and Lunario are true hold-up horses pushed into a midfield mapping because the rear of the field is oversubscribed — they are unlikely to secure their natural deep position and their finishing kicks may be compromised as a result. This race shape — contested pace, honest gallop, good-to-firm ground — squarely favours late-running hold-up types who can travel wide of trouble and produce a sustained finish, with Desert Shadow and Tavana the horses best placed to capitalise on the speed up front burning itself out.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Burns, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Ascending Star and Thursday Girl fight it out up front and set a tempo that stretches the field from the first furlong, leaving the pace-setters spent inside the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: The contested lead creates the classic setup for hold-up horses to sweep past fading front-runners in the closing stages on Sandown's stiff finish; this is the most natural outcome given the confirmed duel for the lead. Desert Shadow's strong form at similar distances on good ground and Tavana's recent 7f win make them the prime beneficiaries of this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Settles, Front Wins
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two front-runners concedes early and allows the other to control a more measured gallop, conserving enough to hold on.
scenarios.body: A solo leader able to dictate their own rhythm at a sustainable pace on good-to-firm Sandown turf retains enough in reserve to repel closing runners over the final furlong; Thursday Girl's recent win and consistent placed form at this trip makes her the more likely beneficiary given her trainer's excellent 14-day strike rate. Ascending Star is equally capable of filling this role given her course-friendly profile.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Duo Strike Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is truly fierce, opening up an unusually large gap and allowing the redistributed midfield runners to close with purpose from a better-than-usual position.
scenarios.body: Sunny Smile and Lunario, though mapped to midfield rather than their natural hold-up berths, could still finish strongly if the pace truly collapses; however, racing out of their preferred deep role tempers this scenario's likelihood significantly. Sunny Smile's consistent placed form at 7f on good ground and Lunario's recent win at the trip give them residual claims if the shape falls unusually kindly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Mess, No Clear Winner
scenarios.trigger: If early scrimmaging disrupts all horses' rhythms, the pace becomes uneven and the race turns into a messy sprint for home with no clean winner profile.
scenarios.body: An unsettled early gallop could neutralise both the pace-setters and the late runners, producing a chaotic finish where positional luck and a clean run become decisive; this scenario has low probability given the straightforward nature of the split between two clear front-runners and two clear hold-up horses. Ascending Star or Thursday Girl, if they avoid the worst of any interference, would be best placed to capitalise from their forward position.

watchPoints.text: Watch Ascending Star and Thursday Girl in the opening two furlongs — if both refuse to give ground the pace could become genuinely fierce, dramatically increasing the chances of the hold-up horses sweeping past late.

Desert Shadow carries the highest weight in the field at 142lbs on what is effectively good-to-firm ground — monitor whether the combination of top weight and a strong gallop blunts his late acceleration in the final furlong.

Sunny Smile and Lunario are both natural hold-up horses who will struggle to find their preferred deep position — watch whether they can slot in behind the pace or are forced to race too prominently for their style, materially affecting their finishing runs.

Thursday Girl's trainer Ed Walker holds a strong 10/38 T14 record — if she settles into an uncontested lead early after Ascending Star fades from the duel, her in-form yard angle becomes a live upgrading factor.

races.name: Community Fund For Elmbridge Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Kodi Fire
runners_data.note: Recent winner over this course and trip on Good going, and a repeat of that effort is feasible from a prominent position; Charles Hills has a solid T14 strike rate of 3/21, headgear (tp) is retained, and 13 days since last run is a fresh enough gap — the profile is competitive if he settles just off the contested pace.
runners_data.comment: Kodi Fire showed fair form when second last time out and a winner two starts back, giving him some recent credibility, but he ranks fifth of six on our figures and has looked inconsistent in recent starts — hard to fancy at the bottom of the market.

runners_data.name: Bubbles Wonky
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who will press for the lead from the outset, but her form figures of 333 in her last three runs on Standard and Good suggest she finds a rival or two too strong when it matters; trainer Mark Pattinson's T14 read of 0/5 is uninspiring, and she has limited wins on similar ground.
runners_data.comment: Bubbles Wonky has been knocking persistently on the door, finishing third in three consecutive starts, and he returns on a quick 13-day turnaround with experience of today's trip and conditions; our rating of 81 marks him the one to beat, though he remains yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: H Key Lails
runners_data.note: Carries the pace angle with genuine recent winning form (1/7f/GOO latest), and jockey James Glennon claiming 7lb gives a weight advantage worth noting; headgear (p) retained, and trainer Attwater has 1/15 over 14 days — needs to get a clear lead to be effective, but faces a determined rival in Bubbles Wonky for that role.
runners_data.comment: H Key Lails won three starts back and has experience of today's trip and conditions, so the tools are there — stall one, 134 lb, and two sevenths in his last two outings are the obvious concerns.

runners_data.name: Great Blasket
runners_data.note: Last-time-out winner over this exact course and distance on Good ground makes this the standout positive angle; Oisin Murphy takes the ride for a trainer firing at 13/58 in the 14-day window, headgear (v) is familiar, and 7 days between runs is tight but the form is fresh — ideally suited if the front-runners set a true gallop.
runners_data.comment: Great Blasket franked his recent win with a return just seven days ago, and he has experience of both today's trip and going; drawn in stall four carrying 133 lb, our rating of 77 marks him out as a genuine threat — though that quick turnaround is the one factor to watch.

runners_data.name: War Chant
runners_data.note: Reverts to 1m after two runs over longer trips at Southwell, and the return to a sharp Good to Firm mile at Sandown looks the key conditional factor; David Probert is booked but the trainer's T14 of 0/10 offers little encouragement, and his best efforts have come at this distance on similar ground — needs a strong pace to run onto.

runners_data.name: Amused
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner whose form figures include two second-place finishes at this trip on Good going, showing consistency without converting; the 0W record across five recent runs and a trainer T14 of 2/11 suggests the talent is there to be placed but the horse needs everything to fall right — a true-run pace is a prerequisite.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Amused is hard to fancy despite carrying a manageable weight of 129 lb from stall 5; a second last time out and experience over today's distance and going are the slim positives here.

races.paceDynamic: H Key Lails and Bubbles Wonky are both confirmed front-runners, meaning this race opens with a genuine battle for the lead from the gates at Sandown's 1m trip, which starts on the round course and involves a descent into the straight. That contested early pace on Good to Firm ground should produce an honest, even gallop rather than a dawdle, with neither leader likely to surrender the advantage without a fight. The pace duel will put pressure on both front-runners through the middle stages, burning energy that hold-up and midfield horses can preserve before the straight. This race shape squarely favours hold-up and late-finishing profiles, as the contested lead saps the pace-setters and creates a true-run race where those dropping in from behind — particularly Great Blasket and Amused — can exploit the vacated ground in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead Burns Pace
scenarios.trigger: If H Key Lails and Bubbles Wonky fight for the front, setting a genuine gallop that drains both by the straight.
scenarios.body: The pace duel runs the leaders into the ground over the final furlong, leaving the race open for hold-up horses sweeping through on the outside; Good to Firm ground rewards those with a clean turn of foot off a genuine pace. Great Blasket, recent winner over this course and distance, and Amused, who has hit the frame repeatedly at this trip on similar going, are ideally positioned to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Survives
scenarios.trigger: If the pace duel between the two leaders burns itself out early enough for a prominent racer to swoop and inherit a winning position without doing all the work.
scenarios.body: Kodi Fire, tracking just off the pace in the prominent position, avoids the worst of the early scrapping and times a run to hit the front entering the final furlong; with headgear fitted (tp) and a recent win over this course and distance, the profile fits. War Chant could also benefit tracking a sound pace on ground he handles.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two pace-setters gains a clear early lead and the other capitulates, allowing a controlled solo gallop from the front.
scenarios.body: H Key Lails, whose trainer has a 1/15 14-day strike rate and who carries headgear (p), has recent winning form and the tactical nous from jockey James Glennon to press on if Bubbles Wonky is outrun early; a lone leader controlling fractions on Good to Firm could hold on. Bubbles Wonky is the alternative if she breaks sharper and Glennon elects to shadow rather than fight.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Outpaced
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses and the race becomes falsely run, denying deep hold-up horses a true test and favouring handier types.
scenarios.body: A muddled tempo with both leaders backing off each other would compress the field and rob Great Blasket and Amused of the sustained gallop they need to unleash their finishes; in that scenario prominent horses that are close enough to take advantage of a sprint finish hold the edge. This is the least likely shape given the confirmed determination of both front-runners.

watchPoints.text: H Key Lails and Bubbles Wonky: watch the opening two furlongs closely — if neither concedes the lead, the resulting pace war could dramatically inflate the winning chance of Great Blasket and Amused tracking from behind.
Great Blasket ran only 7 days ago; monitor the market for any signs of freshness concerns, as a quick turnaround on Good to Firm ground can dull the finishing kick of a hold-up horse.

Kodi Fire's headgear (tp) and recent course-and-distance win make him dangerous from a prominent position, but if the pace is slower than expected he may be drawn into a sprint finish where his profile is less decisive.

Oisin Murphy's booking for Great Blasket is a notable stable upgrade signal — track his positioning in the early stages, as Murphy is likely to hunt the rail and maximise ground on this turning track.

War Chant's return from two runs at Southwell over longer trips back to Sandown 1m is the trip/course switch worth monitoring; if he shows early toe to race prominently rather than midfield, his chance improves materially under a true pace.
